# Resource: stripe_core_account_person

A person of an account created through Stripe's `/v2` Accounts API, such as its representative, an executive, an owner or a director. `terraform destroy` deletes the person, and changing `account_id` creates a new one. Stripe never returns the `value` of an ID number, so state keeps the values you configured and treats them as sensitive. State holds only the ID numbers you configured, matched by `type`: a minute or two after it creates a person with a `us_ssn_last_4`, Stripe also lists a `us_ssn`, which the data source shows and the resource leaves out. A plan that changes `id_numbers` on an existing person fails, because changing them is not supported yet: revert the configuration, ignore the change, or recreate the person deliberately with `terraform taint` (`tofu taint` in OpenTofu). Stripe returns `address.country` in upper case and a whole `relationship.percent_ownership` with `.0`, so state keeps the values as you configured them. Stripe has no proven way to clear a person's details, so an apply that removes `given_name`, `surname`, `email`, `phone`, `date_of_birth`, `address` or `relationship` from the configuration fails; removing a member of `address` or `relationship` leaves its value on the person.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Stripe's test values for a person who always verifies. In live mode, pass the person's
# identity numbers from sensitive variables.
resource "stripe_core_account_person" "owner" {
  account_id = stripe_core_account.seller.id
  given_name = "Owen"
  surname    = "Rosen"
  email      = "owen.rosen@example.com"
  phone      = "0000000000"

  date_of_birth = {
    day   = 1
    month = 1
    year  = 1901
  }

  address = {
    line1       = "address_full_match"
    city        = "South San Francisco"
    state       = "CA"
    postal_code = "94080"
    country     = "US"
  }

  id_numbers = [
    { type = "us_ssn_last_4", value = "0000" },
  ]

  relationship = {
    owner             = true
    percent_ownership = "60"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `account_id` - (Required) The ID of the parent object. Changing it replaces the resource.

The following arguments are optional:

* `address` - (Optional) The person's residential address. See [`address`](#address) below.
* `date_of_birth` - (Optional) The person's date of birth. See [`date_of_birth`](#date_of_birth) below.
* `email` - (Optional) Email.
* `given_name` - (Optional) The person's first name.
* `id_numbers` - (Optional) The identification numbers (e.g., SSN) associated with the person. See [`id_numbers`](#id_numbers) below.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of key-value pairs that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `phone` - (Optional) The phone number for this person.
* `relationship` - (Optional) The relationship that this person has with the Account's business or legal entity. See [`relationship`](#relationship) below.
* `surname` - (Optional) The person's last name.

<a id="address"></a>
### `address`

The `address` attribute supports:

* `city` - (Optional) City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - (Required) Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - (Optional) Address line 1 (e.g., street, PO Box, or company name).
* `line2` - (Optional) Address line 2 (e.g., apartment, suite, unit, or building).
* `postal_code` - (Optional) ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - (Optional) State, county, province, or region.

<a id="date_of_birth"></a>
### `date_of_birth`

The `date_of_birth` attribute supports:

* `day` - (Required) The day of birth.
* `month` - (Required) The month of birth.
* `year` - (Required) The year of birth.

<a id="id_numbers"></a>
### `id_numbers`

The `id_numbers` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `type` - (Required) The ID number type of an individual. Possible values: `ae_eid`, `ao_nif`, `ar_cuil`, `ar_dni`, `at_stn`, `az_tin`, `bd_brc`, `bd_etin`, `bd_nid`, `be_nrn`, `bg_ucn`, `bn_nric`, `br_cpf`, `ca_sin`, `ch_oasi`, `cl_rut`, `cn_pp`, `co_nuip`, `cr_ci`, `cr_cpf`, `cr_dimex`, `cr_nite`, `cy_tic`, `cz_rc`, `de_stn`, `dk_cpr`, `do_cie`, `do_rcn`, `ec_ci`, `ee_ik`, `es_nif`, `fi_hetu`, `fr_nir`, `gb_nino`, `gr_afm`, `gt_nit`, `hk_id`, `hr_oib`, `hu_ad`, `id_nik`, `ie_ppsn`, `is_kt`, `it_cf`, `jp_inc`, `ke_pin`, `kz_iin`, `li_peid`, `lt_ak`, `lu_nif`, `lv_pk`, `mx_rfc`, `my_nric`, `mz_nuit`, `ng_nin`, `nl_bsn`, `no_nin`, `nz_ird`, `pe_dni`, `pk_cnic`, `pk_snic`, `pl_pesel`, `pt_nif`, `ro_cnp`, `sa_tin`, `se_pin`, `sg_fin`, `sg_nric`, `sk_dic`, `th_lc`, `th_pin`, `tr_tin`, `us_itin`, `us_itin_last_4`, `us_ssn`, `us_ssn_last_4`, `uy_dni`, `za_id`.
* `value` - (Required, Sensitive) The value of the ID number.

<a id="relationship"></a>
### `relationship`

The `relationship` attribute supports:

* `authorizer` - (Read-Only) Whether the individual is an authorizer of the Account's identity.
* `director` - (Optional) Indicates whether the person is a director of the associated legal entity.
* `executive` - (Optional) Indicates whether the person is an executive of the associated legal entity.
* `legal_guardian` - (Read-Only) Whether the individual is the legal guardian of the Account's representative.
* `owner` - (Optional) Indicates whether the person is an owner of the associated legal entity.
* `percent_ownership` - (Optional) The percentage of ownership the person has in the associated legal entity.
* `representative` - (Optional) Indicates whether the person is a representative of the associated legal entity.
* `title` - (Optional) The title or position the person holds in the associated legal entity.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the Person.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Represented as a RFC 3339 date & time UTC value in millisecond precision, for example: 2022-09-18T13:22:18.123Z.
* `livemode` - Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.
* `updated` - Time at which the object was last updated. Represented as a RFC 3339 date & time UTC value in millisecond precision, for example: 2022-09-18T13:22:18.123Z.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Import

The ID is the account ID and the person ID, separated by a slash.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a core account person using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_core_account_person.owner
  id = "acct_1Nv0FGQ9RKHgCVdK/person_test_61TfDy4hQtjfXq8Y2nVrPw3bKcLmZsAe9uHgJdNo5RiW"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_core_account_person.owner
  identity = {
    account_id = "acct_1Nv0FGQ9RKHgCVdK"
    id         = "person_test_61TfDy4hQtjfXq8Y2nVrPw3bKcLmZsAe9uHgJdNo5RiW"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `account_id` (String) The ID of the parent account id.
* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the core account person.

Using `terraform import`, import a core account person using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_core_account_person.owner acct_1Nv0FGQ9RKHgCVdK/person_test_61TfDy4hQtjfXq8Y2nVrPw3bKcLmZsAe9uHgJdNo5RiW
```

~> Stripe never returns the `value` of an ID number, so an imported person has none in `id_numbers`, and its `address.country` and `relationship.percent_ownership` are as Stripe returns them. Add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [id_numbers] }` to a configuration that sets them, because a plan that changes `id_numbers` fails.
